value.value: Decisions about the art language itself — what it is for, its scope, and its syntax/semantics model.

The project had several candidate scopes (tasks domain, language spec, tooling). Work on all of them at once would spread effort before the core was proven; the tasks domain was only ever an example use case.
) is the first scope and the first test case for the bundling pipeline. Work on any other domain is deferred until the spec and pipeline are proven.
Art could be positioned in many ways; without a defined core, new candidates (drift-checks, etc.) keep expanding scope and diluting design.

Art has two main use cases: (1) generating agent instructions, and (2) acting as a single source of truth for declarations that are both machine-readable and human/agent-readable. Everything else (context minimisation, fewer contradictions, automated SoT→instructions, portability) is a benefit of these two, not a separate use case.
The grammar needs an extensibility model without becoming an ouroboros (spec reading spec). Extensibility at the grammar layer would fragment parsing.
Syntax is closed — implemented in TypeScript, no grammar plugins. Semantics are open and data-driven, extensible via
Art sources and plain markdown coexist in the same tree; a hard file-type wall would make existing markdown invalid and block incremental adoption.
Any markdown file is a valid
file. Files not authored in art require more inference to read correctly, but are never invalid.

children.name: Construct Containment and the NaturalBlock Catch-all

value.value: The grammar's containment model was underspecified: FieldBlock values terminated at the next FieldBlock, FieldInline, or InlineDeclaration but not at a SectionBlock, and "arbitrary content" rules allowed circular nesting (a FieldBlock containing a SectionBlock or a nested FieldBlock) that carries no semantic meaning. Plain Markdown content also lacked an explicit classification home.

Containment is explicit. SectionBlocks MAY nest (heading level drives nesting). A FieldBlock value terminates at the next FieldBlock, FieldInline, InlineDeclaration, SectionBlock, or the end of the enclosing SectionBlock, and MUST NOT contain a SectionBlock or a nested FieldBlock. NaturalBlock is the catch-all classification: any content that does not match another construct is a NaturalBlock — realising "Any Markdown is Valid

Termination signals become unambiguous for the construct-stack parser; classification is total (every token stream classifies into a record); per-position content unions in the record schema mirror the containment model. (construct-stack pattern: see

Domain records and other artefacts are expressed as markdown files. Rendering them into per-consumer projections requires templates that carry both deterministic operations (iteration over data sets, field interpolation) and natural-language instructions agents can process; without a dedicated template language that logic leaks into hand-maintained code or duplicated outputs.
as a template engine with flat, inline directive syntax, so
sources stay readable and editable in any markdown-capable editor. Generators compile
templates into the markdown projections consumers read.

children.name: SectionBlock as the Resource Declaration Carrier

value.value: + tags + content) is what turns a markdown heading into a named, kinded resource, but the grammar spec described it only as "a named structural section" — opaque, and hiding the connection between the grammar and modules layers. Without an explicit statement of its role, the Closed Syntax, Open Semantics split reads as abstract: it is unclear which parts of a declaration the language fixes and which parts domains provide. The programming-language precedent makes the intended model obvious in hindsight:
is fixed syntax; the meaning of
comes from the program. Art needs the equivalent — a fixed construct form whose kinds are open.
The SectionBlock is the resource declaration carrier:

declares a resource of that kind with that name. The construct's form (optional kind, name, tags, content) is fixed by the grammar — closed syntax. The meaning of each kind is provided by the structures, the domain declarations in
— open semantics. The grammar and modules layers meet exactly here.

The parser captures declarations generically: it needs to know only that a resource of kind K named N is declared, never what K means. Domain semantics (fields, constraints, routines) attach to kinds through structures, keeping the core grammar frozen. The construct spec must state this purpose so the grammar-to-modules connection is explicit rather than implied.

The grammar spec files described containment loosely. The mdast-based parser implements explicit containment rules that need to be reflected in the spec.

SectionBlocks nest by heading level. FieldBlock values terminate at the next FieldBlock, SectionBlock, or end of enclosing SectionBlock. NaturalBlock is the catch-all for any unclassified content. Tags are detected in prose via regex, not in code blocks.
The spec files now match the parser implementation. The containment model is unambiguous for both parsers and spec readers.
